title: Gartner forecasts over 40% of agentic AI projects cancelled by end of 2027, signalling infrastructure ahead of product-market fit
content:
The skeptical counterweight to agentic-economy enthusiasm (per LI.FI):

- **Gartner (June 2025): more than 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end of 2027**, citing escalating costs, unclear business value, and inadequate risk controls
- Consumer-facing agentic applications have **not achieved product-market fit** despite infrastructure maturation
- **Legal gap:** the Amazon v. Perplexity ruling highlighted the absence of legal clarity for agentic authorization, with no alternative pathways established

**Why it matters:** the rails (payments, identity, intents) are ahead of demand; value capture will concentrate in use cases with objectively verifiable outcomes rather than open-ended consumer delegation.

Source: LI.FI, "The Agentic Economy — A Deep Dive" (https://li.fi/knowledge-hub/the-agentic-economy-%E2%80%94-a-deep-dive).

## Boundary: the bull and bear cases measure different things
These two forecasts are routinely read as contradictory and are not. McKinsey sizes a **market** in 2030; Gartner counts **project mortality** by end-2027. A shakeout that kills more than 40% of initiatives while the surviving use cases compound into trillions is the ordinary shape of an infrastructure build-out, not a paradox — and both sources agree on the mechanism, that the rails are ahead of demand and value concentrates where outcomes are objectively verifiable.

What the pair does establish is that **neither number is settled**: the vault should carry them as a scenario range, not as a projection. The discriminating evidence is B2B adoption data in 2027-2028, which is when the two forecasts stop being compatible — if enterprise orchestration has not compounded by then, the bear case was the base case.
description: Escalating costs, unclear business value, and weak risk controls drive cancellations; consumer agentic apps lack PMF despite mature payment rails. Legal clarity also absent.
